text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition politician Tang Liang Hong says he will appeal against High Court's decision to strike out his defence in defamation suits brought against him by ruling People's Action Party.
- Tang says he might consider seeking asylum abroad.
- Explosion at nuclear fuel reprocessing plant northeast of Tokyo might have released radioactive material.
- Dog-beater jailed in landmark cruelty case.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore relaxes disclosure requirements regarding directors' pay packages.
- Keppel Corp announces 4.7 percent dip in 1996 net profit to Singapore $204.1 million and proposes one-for-four bonus issue of new shares.
- IPC Corp tries to clarify questions raised about its 1996 financial results.
- Listing of Raffles Medical Group has doctors concerned over need to balance commercial interests against provision of quality patient care.
- Thai stocks surge as cabinet okays property bail-out plan.
- Acer Computer International's profit growth slows to 4.7 percent in 1996 with Singapore $32.5 million net profit.
- Keppel Fels Ltd falls 10.4 percent on 1996 results.
- Paper and packaging maker New Toyo International Holdings secures in-principle approval from stock exchange for mainboard listing.
- Japanese trading house Itochu Corp to buy stake in Singapore-based Asia Pulp and Paper Co Ltd for U.S. $1 million.
- IPC Corp's backdating of subsidiaries' disposals puzzles analysts.
